title: Swap and swappiness
subtitle: Overflow RAM to disk; sizing and activation — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Disk space used as overflow when RAM is full — inactive pages are moved to swap
cards.notes: Helps machines with little RAM. Not a replacement for more RAM — disk (even SSD) is slower than memory.

cards.meaning: Btrfs does not support swap space
cards.example: do not put swap on Btrfs
cards.notes: Use another filesystem or a dedicated partition/file elsewhere.

cards.meaning: Dedicated swap partition, swap file, or a combination of both
cards.notes: From the OS’s point of view all are just swap devices/files.

cards.meaning: Red Hat recommends swap partitions — contiguous area on HDD for better throughput/seek
cards.notes: Partition = recommended / simpler for the kernel. File = flexible / no repartitioning.

cards.meaning: Flexible swap: any size, on any mounted filesystem, without repartitioning
cards.notes: From kernel 2.6 onward, virtually as fast as partitions if allocated contiguously — kernel maps blocks and accesses the device directly.

cards.meaning: List active swap devices/files
cards.notes: Verify after swapon.

cards.meaning: Show RAM and swap usage in human-readable units
cards.notes: Pairs with /proc/swaps for a quick check.

cards.meaning: Kernel parameter: relative weight of swapping cold anonymous pages vs dropping page cache when free RAM cannot satisfy an allocation
cards.notes: High = happy to swap. Low = protect application RAM, throw away file cache first.

cards.meaning: 0–100 inclusive
cards.notes: Default is 60 — fine for most workloads.
Fine for most workloads.

cards.meaning: Prefer evicting page cache; keep apps in RAM → more consistent low latency
cards.example: desktops, interactive boxes with plenty of RAM
cards.notes: Desktops may want it lower.

cards.meaning: Prefer swapping cold app pages → can increase throughput (especially disk I/O) but risk latency spikes
cards.example: batch / less interactive systems may want it higher
cards.notes: Pages needed again can cause latency spikes.

cards.meaning: Recommended swap = 2 × RAM; with hibernation = 3 × RAM
cards.example: 1 GB RAM → 2 GB swap (3 GB if hibernating)
cards.notes: From RHEL 7 Storage Administration Guide table.

cards.front: RHEL 7 swap size: RAM > 2 GB – 8 GB
cards.meaning: Recommended swap = equal to RAM; with hibernation = 2 × RAM
cards.example: 4 GB RAM → 4 GB swap (8 GB if hibernating)
cards.notes: Hibernation needs swap at least as large as RAM (table uses more than 1× as safety).

cards.front: RHEL 7 swap size: RAM > 8 GB – 64 GB
cards.meaning: Recommended swap = at least 4 GB; with hibernation = 1.5 × RAM
cards.example: 16 GB RAM → ≥ 4 GB swap (24 GB if hibernating)
cards.notes: Know the table for this course.

cards.meaning: Recommended swap = at least 4 GB; hibernation not recommended
cards.notes: Modern huge-RAM systems may size by workload (~20% of RAM as a later rule of thumb).

cards.meaning: Hibernation writes RAM out to swap — swap must be at least as large as RAM
cards.example: table uses more than 1× as a safety margin
cards.notes: Above 64 GB RAM, hibernation is not recommended in the RHEL 7 table.

cards.meaning: lvcreate → mkswap → fstab → systemctl daemon-reload → swapon
cards.notes: Never mkfs.ext4 on a swap LV.

cards.meaning: Create the LV that will hold swap
cards.notes: Example path: /dev/VolGroup00/LogVol02.

cards.meaning: Format a device or file as swap (not mkfs)
cards.notes: Puts a swap signature on the LV or file.

cards.meaning: Enable swap at boot: device/file, type swap, defaults 0 0
cards.notes: Same pattern for /swapfile swap swap defaults 0 0.

cards.meaning: Reread fstab into systemd after adding or removing a swap line
cards.notes: Used after fstab changes for both add and remove flows.

cards.meaning: Activate a swap device or file now
cards.notes: swapon /swapfile for a file. -v is verbose in the LV example.

cards.front: dd for a 64 MB swap file
cards.meaning: Create an empty file: bs=1024, count = size_in_MB × 1024
Lock down permissions — swap file must not be world-readable
cards.notes: May hold RAM secrets.

cards.meaning: swapoff → remove fstab line → daemon-reload → rm
cards.notes: Never rm an active swap file.

cards.meaning: Deactivate a swap device or file before deleting it
cards.notes: Required before rm of an active swap file.
